endorsements.quote: There is also a need to ensure that objective and transparent confidence metrics are built into such processes, to reduce the risk of automation bias, i.e. clinician overconfidence in case formulations generated by such agents.

As such, it is important that practising clinicians and users of mental health services – not just those with an understanding of technology – are involved in the development of the new computational tools.

unlisted_practices: Develop a consensus governance framework for the responsible use of generative AI in mental healthcare that maps existing AI governance principles.
Ensure clinicians have significant and sufficient agentive reach into the finalisation of AI-generated case formulations.
Develop confidence metrics and paradigms using explainable AI protocols for mental health AI tools as an urgent task.
Prepare clinicians to explain AI confidence metrics and their meaning to patients.
Require developers of LLM-based mental health clinical technologies to demonstrate governance principles and measures across each domain of the CRITiCS framework.
Develop objective measures of clinician agentive reach into automated clinical systems.
Involve mental health service users as equal partners in the development of AI tools.
Ensure AI models represent the ontological status of mental health constructs transparently.
Protect against overemphasis of weak signals by AI that leads to overtreatment and stigmatisation.
Train clinicians in weak signal principles and in constructing effective interrogations of LLM outputs.

screen.reason: This paper presents a conceptual framework (CRITiCS) offering recommendations and guidance for the safe deployment and clinician oversight of generative AI in mental health decision-making.
